claim: At physiological protein levels, the slow HOPS- and SNARE-dependent fusion which occurs upon complete SNARE zippering is stimulated by Sec17 and Sec18:ATP without requiring ATP hydrolysis.
source: At physiological protein levels, the slow HOPS- and SNARE-dependent fusion which occurs upon complete SNARE zippering is stimulated by Sec17 and Sec18:ATP without requiring ATP hydrolysis.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A, where fusion with ATPγS (non-hydrolyzable) is nearly as rapid as with ATP for the first 10 minutes.

claim: Sec17 needs its central residues which bind the 0-layer of the SNARE complex for stimulation.
source: To stimulate, Sec17 needs its central residues which bind the 0-layer of the SNARE complex and its N-terminal apolar loop.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 3A showing that the Sec17-K159E,K163E mutation (which interferes with SNARE 0-layer interactions) reduces fusion to levels seen without Sec17.

claim: Sec17 needs its N-terminal apolar loop for stimulation.
source: To stimulate, Sec17 needs its central residues which bind the 0-layer of the SNARE complex and its N-terminal apolar loop.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 3A showing that the Sec17-F21S,M22S mutation (which removes apolar character of the N-loop) reduces fusion.

claim: Adding a transmembrane anchor to the N-terminus of Sec17 bypasses the requirement for apolarity of the Sec17 loop.
source: Adding a transmembrane anchor to the N-terminus of Sec17 bypasses this requirement for apolarity of the Sec17 loop, suggesting that the loop functions for membrane binding rather than to trigger bilayer rearrangement.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4 showing that TM-Sec17-F21S,M22S shows similar stimulation of fusion activity as TM-Sec17 wild-type.

claim: The Sec17 apolar loop functions for membrane binding rather than to trigger bilayer rearrangement when complete C-terminal SNARE zippering occurs.
source: Adding a transmembrane anchor to the N-terminus of Sec17 bypasses this requirement for apolarity of the Sec17 loop, suggesting that the loop functions for membrane binding rather than to trigger bilayer rearrangement.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observation that TM-anchored Sec17 bypasses the need for the apolar loop.

claim: When complete C-terminal SNARE zippering is prevented, fusion strictly requires Sec18 and Sec17.
source: In contrast, when complete C-terminal SNARE zippering is prevented, fusion strictly requires Sec18 and Sec17, and the Sec17 apolar loop has functions beyond membrane anchoring.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 5B showing that fusion with Qc-3Δ is lost upon omission of either Sec17 or Sec18.

claim: When complete C-terminal SNARE zippering is prevented, the Sec17 apolar loop has functions beyond membrane anchoring.
source: In contrast, when complete C-terminal SNARE zippering is prevented, fusion strictly requires Sec18 and Sec17, and the Sec17 apolar loop has functions beyond membrane anchoring.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 6C showing that with Qc-3Δ, TM-Sec17 F21S,M22S shows diminished fusion compared to TM-Sec17 wild-type, indicating the apolar loop provides more than membrane anchoring.

claim: Sec17 and Sec18 act twice in the fusion cycle: binding to trans-SNARE complexes to accelerate fusion, then hydrolyzing ATP to disassemble cis-SNARE complexes.
source: Thus Sec17 and Sec18 act twice in the fusion cycle, binding to trans-SNARE complexes to accelerate fusion, then hydrolyzing ATP to disassemble cis-SNARE complexes.
evidence: This is supported by data showing fusion stimulation without ATP hydrolysis (Figure 2A) and ATP-dependent cis-SNARE disassembly (Figure 2B).

claim: Membrane fusion is essential for each stage of inter-organelle trafficking.
source: Membrane fusion is essential for each stage of inter-organelle trafficking.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge in the field of cell biology.

claim: Fusion requires lipids and proteins which are conserved among the exocytic and endocytic organelles, and in organisms from yeast to humans.
source: Fusion requires lipids and proteins which are conserved among the exocytic and endocytic organelles, and in organisms from yeast to humans.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by extensive literature in the field.

claim: The Rab/Ypt family GTPases are activated for fusion by nucleotide exchange to their GTP-bound state, then bind effector proteins.
source: The Rab/Ypt family GTPases are activated for fusion by nucleotide exchange to their GTP-bound state, then bind effector proteins (Grosshans et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Grosshans et al., 2006.

claim: Some Rab/Ypt effectors are large multisubunit tethering complexes.
source: Some effectors are large multisubunit tethering complexes (Yu and Hughson, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yu and Hughson, 2010.

claim: SNAREs are defined by their heptad-repeat SNARE domains, which can assemble into a 4-helical coiled coil SNARE complex.
source: SNAREs are defined by their heptad-repeat SNARE domains, which can assemble into a 4-helical coiled coil SNARE complex (Jahn and Scheller, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Jahn and Scheller, 2006.

claim: Many SNAREs have a C-terminal hydrophobic membrane anchor.
source: Many SNAREs have a C-terminal hydrophobic membrane anchor.
evidence: This is established knowledge about SNARE protein structure.

claim: In the SNARE domains of the quaternary SNARE complex, polar aminoacyl residues face the exterior.
source: In the SNARE domains of the quaternary SNARE complex, polar aminoacyl residues face the exterior.
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about SNARE complexes.

claim: The interior of the 4-SNARE coiled coil is largely comprised of apolar residues.
source: Though the interior of the 4-SNARE coiled coil is largely comprised of apolar residues, each SNARE has an arginyl (R) or glutaminyl (Q) residue at the center of its SNARE domain, facing each other in the center and interior of the 4-SNARE complex.
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about SNARE complexes.

claim: Each SNARE has an arginyl (R) or glutaminyl (Q) residue at the center of its SNARE domain, facing each other in the center and interior of the 4-SNARE complex.
source: Though the interior of the 4-SNARE coiled coil is largely comprised of apolar residues, each SNARE has an arginyl (R) or glutaminyl (Q) residue at the center of its SNARE domain, facing each other in the center and interior of the 4-SNARE complex.
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about SNARE complexes.

claim: SNAREs are in 4 conserved families, and SNARE complexes are comprised of one SNARE from each of the R, Qa, Qb, and Qc families.
source: SNAREs are in 4 conserved families, and SNARE complexes are comprised of one SNARE from each of the R, Qa, Qb, and Qc families (Fasshauer et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Fasshauer et al., 1998.

claim: SNARE complex assembly is catalyzed by SM (Sec1-Munc18) family proteins.
source: SNARE complex assembly is catalyzed by SM (Sec1-Munc18) family proteins (Rizo and Südhof, 2012; Baker et al., 2015; Orr et al., 2017), and disassembly is catalyzed by the ATP-driven chaperone Sec18 (NSF), aided by its co-chaperone Sec17 (αSNAP) (Söllner et al., 1993; Mayer et al., 1996; Ungermann et al., 1998; Cipriano et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Rizo and Südhof, 2012; Baker et al., 2015; Orr et al., 2017.

claim: SNARE complex disassembly is catalyzed by the ATP-driven chaperone Sec18 (NSF), aided by its co-chaperone Sec17 (αSNAP).
source: SNARE complex assembly is catalyzed by SM (Sec1-Munc18) family proteins (Rizo and Südhof, 2012; Baker et al., 2015; Orr et al., 2017), and disassembly is catalyzed by the ATP-driven chaperone Sec18 (NSF), aided by its co-chaperone Sec17 (αSNAP) (Söllner et al., 1993; Mayer et al., 1996; Ungermann et al., 1998; Cipriano et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Söllner et al., 1993; Mayer et al., 1996; Ungermann et al., 1998; Cipriano et al., 2013.

claim: A tethering factor can bind to Rab GTPases on two membranes as a first step towards fusion.
source: A tethering factor can bind to Rab GTPases on two membranes as a first step towards fusion (Hickey and Wickner, 2010; Miller et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hickey and Wickner, 2010; Miller et al., 2013.

claim: SM proteins can catalyze trans-SNARE complex assembly.
source: SM proteins, which may be bound to a Rab's effectors, can then catalyze trans-SNARE complex assembly (reviewed in Baker and Hughson, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Baker and Hughson, 2016 review.

claim: Four SNARE domains 'zipper' together from N- to C-, drawing the membranes together so closely as to exclude other membrane-surface proteins and bring the lipid polar head groups into direct apposition.
source: Four SNARE domains 'zipper' together from N- to C-, drawing the membranes together so closely as to exclude other membrane-surface proteins and bring the lipid polar head groups into direct apposition.
evidence: This is established knowledge about SNARE-mediated membrane fusion.

claim: The formation of continuous α-helices between the SNARE domains and their trans-membrane anchors has been proposed to stress the bilayers to induce fusion.
source: The formation of continuous α-helices between the SNARE domains and their trans-membrane anchors has been proposed to stress the bilayers to induce fusion (Hanson et al., 1997a, 1997b; Stein et al., 2009), yet yeast vacuole and neuronal synaptic fusion can occur with SNAREs that are prenyl-anchored and lack trans-membrane helices (Xu et al., 2011; Zhou et al., 2013) and even tethering membranes through DNA with lipid anchors at each end can lead to measurable fusion (Chan et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hanson et al., 1997a, 1997b; Stein et al., 2009.

claim: Yeast vacuole and neuronal synaptic fusion can occur with SNAREs that are prenyl-anchored and lack trans-membrane helices.
source: The formation of continuous α-helices between the SNARE domains and their trans-membrane anchors has been proposed to stress the bilayers to induce fusion (Hanson et al., 1997a, 1997b; Stein et al., 2009), yet yeast vacuole and neuronal synaptic fusion can occur with SNAREs that are prenyl-anchored and lack trans-membrane helices (Xu et al., 2011; Zhou et al., 2013) and even tethering membranes through DNA with lipid anchors at each end can lead to measurable fusion (Chan et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Xu et al., 2011; Zhou et al., 2013.

claim: Tethering membranes through DNA with lipid anchors at each end can lead to measurable fusion.
source: The formation of continuous α-helices between the SNARE domains and their trans-membrane anchors has been proposed to stress the bilayers to induce fusion (Hanson et al., 1997a, 1997b; Stein et al., 2009), yet yeast vacuole and neuronal synaptic fusion can occur with SNAREs that are prenyl-anchored and lack trans-membrane helices (Xu et al., 2011; Zhou et al., 2013) and even tethering membranes through DNA with lipid anchors at each end can lead to measurable fusion (Chan et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Chan et al., 2008.

claim: Full SNARE zippering may promote fusion through close apposition of bilayers.
source: Full SNARE zippering may also promote fusion though close apposition of bilayers, and by serving as a platform to bind other proteins which trigger the lipid rearrangements of fusion, such as Sec17 (Zick et al., 2015) or synaptotagmin (Fernández-Chacón et al., 2001).
evidence: This is speculative reasoning about mechanisms of SNARE-mediated fusion.

claim: Full SNARE zippering may promote fusion by serving as a platform to bind other proteins which trigger the lipid rearrangements of fusion, such as Sec17 or synaptotagmin.
source: Full SNARE zippering may also promote fusion though close apposition of bilayers, and by serving as a platform to bind other proteins which trigger the lipid rearrangements of fusion, such as Sec17 (Zick et al., 2015) or synaptotagmin (Fernández-Chacón et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Zick et al., 2015 and Fernández-Chacón et al., 2001.

claim: The vacuolar tethering complex HOPS has 6 subunits.
source: The vacuolar tethering complex HOPS (homotypic fusion and vacuole protein sorting) has 6 subunits (Seals et al., 2000), two which bind to the Ypt7:GTP vacuolar Rab (Brett et al., 2008; Plemel et al., 2011; Bröcker et al., 2012) to perform tethering (Hickey and Wickner, 2010) and one (Vps33) which is the SM protein of that organelle.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Seals et al., 2000.

claim: Two HOPS subunits bind to the Ypt7:GTP vacuolar Rab to perform tethering.
source: The vacuolar tethering complex HOPS (homotypic fusion and vacuole protein sorting) has 6 subunits (Seals et al., 2000), two which bind to the Ypt7:GTP vacuolar Rab (Brett et al., 2008; Plemel et al., 2011; Bröcker et al., 2012) to perform tethering (Hickey and Wickner, 2010) and one (Vps33) which is the SM protein of that organelle.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Brett et al., 2008; Plemel et al., 2011; Bröcker et al., 2012; Hickey and Wickner, 2010.

claim: Vps33 is the SM protein of the vacuole.
source: The vacuolar tethering complex HOPS (homotypic fusion and vacuole protein sorting) has 6 subunits (Seals et al., 2000), two which bind to the Ypt7:GTP vacuolar Rab (Brett et al., 2008; Plemel et al., 2011; Bröcker et al., 2012) to perform tethering (Hickey and Wickner, 2010) and one (Vps33) which is the SM protein of that organelle.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the HOPS complex.

claim: Vps33 has direct affinity for the SNARE domains of the vacuolar R-SNARE Nyv1 and for the Qa SNARE Vam3.
source: Vps33 has direct affinity for the SNARE domains of the vacuolar R-SNARE Nyv1 and for the Qa SNARE Vam3 (Lobingier and Merz, 2012; Baker et al., 2015), enabling HOPS to catalyze the assembly of a complex of the 4 vacuolar SNAREs (Baker et al., 2015; Orr et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lobingier and Merz, 2012; Baker et al., 2015.

claim: HOPS catalyzes the assembly of a complex of the 4 vacuolar SNAREs.
source: Vps33 has direct affinity for the SNARE domains of the vacuolar R-SNARE Nyv1 and for the Qa SNARE Vam3 (Lobingier and Merz, 2012; Baker et al., 2015), enabling HOPS to catalyze the assembly of a complex of the 4 vacuolar SNAREs (Baker et al., 2015; Orr et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Baker et al., 2015; Orr et al., 2017.

claim: The Qc-SNARE Vam7 lacks an integral membrane anchor and is water-soluble.
source: The Qc-SNARE Vam7 lacks an integral membrane anchor and is water-soluble; it binds to the membrane by its affinities for the other SNAREs, for the HOPS subunits Vps16 and Vps18 (Krämer and Ungermann, 2011), and for PtdIns(3)P (Cheever et al., 2001).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Vam7 structure.

claim: Vam7 binds to the membrane by its affinities for the other SNAREs, for the HOPS subunits Vps16 and Vps18, and for PtdIns(3)P.
source: The Qc-SNARE Vam7 lacks an integral membrane anchor and is water-soluble; it binds to the membrane by its affinities for the other SNAREs, for the HOPS subunits Vps16 and Vps18 (Krämer and Ungermann, 2011), and for PtdIns(3)P (Cheever et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Krämer and Ungermann, 2011 and Cheever et al., 2001.

claim: Vacuole fusion has been studied in vivo.
source: Vacuole fusion has been studied in vivo (Wada et al., 1992), with the purified organelle (Wickner, 2010), and as reconstituted into proteoliposomes with all purified components (Mima et al., 2008; Stroupe et al., 2009; Zick and Wickner, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wada et al., 1992.

claim: Vacuole fusion has been studied with the purified organelle.
source: Vacuole fusion has been studied in vivo (Wada et al., 1992), with the purified organelle (Wickner, 2010), and as reconstituted into proteoliposomes with all purified components (Mima et al., 2008; Stroupe et al., 2009; Zick and Wickner, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wickner, 2010.

claim: Vacuole fusion has been reconstituted into proteoliposomes with all purified components.
source: Vacuole fusion has been studied in vivo (Wada et al., 1992), with the purified organelle (Wickner, 2010), and as reconstituted into proteoliposomes with all purified components (Mima et al., 2008; Stroupe et al., 2009; Zick and Wickner, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Mima et al., 2008; Stroupe et al., 2009; Zick and Wickner, 2016.

claim: Schwartz and Merz (2009) found that the fusion of purified vacuoles was lost when complete SNARE zippering was prevented through deletion of 21 amino acyl residues from the C-terminal end of the Qc SNARE Vam7.
source: Schwartz and Merz (2009) found that the fusion of purified vacuoles was lost when complete SNARE zippering was prevented through deletion of 21 amino acyl residues (3 heptad repeats) from the C-terminal and membrane-proximal end of the Qc SNARE Vam7.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Schwartz and Merz, 2009.

claim: Fusion arrested by the Vam7 mutant SNARE could be largely restored by the addition of recombinant Sec17.
source: Fusion arrested by this mutant SNARE could be largely restored by the addition of recombinant Sec17.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Schwartz and Merz, 2009 in the preceding context.

claim: Restoration of fusion by Sec17 with the Vam7 mutant did not require ATP and was insensitive to antibodies to Sec18.
source: Though the targets and mechanism of Sec17 action on the organelle were unclear, restoration did not require ATP and was insensitive to antibodies to Sec18.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Schwartz and Merz, 2009 in the preceding context.

claim: Using purified vacuoles which had docked in vitro, almost all trans-SNARE complexes bore Sec17.
source: A second study, using purified vacuoles which had docked in vitro, found that almost all trans-SNARE complexes bore Sec17 (Xu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Xu et al., 2010.

claim: Sec17 and the HOPS SM subunit Vps33 can cooperatively associate with vacuole SNARE complexes.
source: A third study found that Sec17 and the HOPS SM subunit Vps33 could cooperatively associate with vacuole SNARE complexes (Lobingier et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lobingier et al., 2014.

claim: When lipids had optimal, vacuolar head-group composition and fatty acyl fluidity, Sec17 had only a minor stimulatory effect on HOPS-dependent proteoliposome fusion in the absence of Sec18.
source: A fourth study (Zick et al., 2015) examined the effects of Sec17 on HOPS-dependent proteoliposome fusion in the absence of Sec18 and with high SNARE concentrations. When the lipids had optimal, vacuolar head-group composition and fatty acyl fluidity, Sec17 had only a minor stimulatory effect on fusion, but when fusion was strongly suppressed by alternative lipid compositions, fusion became dependent on Sec17 and on its N-domain apolar loop.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Zick et al., 2015.

claim: When fusion was strongly suppressed by alternative lipid compositions, fusion became dependent on Sec17 and on its N-domain apolar loop.
source: A fourth study (Zick et al., 2015) examined the effects of Sec17 on HOPS-dependent proteoliposome fusion in the absence of Sec18 and with high SNARE concentrations. When the lipids had optimal, vacuolar head-group composition and fatty acyl fluidity, Sec17 had only a minor stimulatory effect on fusion, but when fusion was strongly suppressed by alternative lipid compositions, fusion became dependent on Sec17 and on its N-domain apolar loop.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Zick et al., 2015.

claim: High SNARE levels can bypass and mask many fusion reaction requirements, such as for the Rab and even for HOPS.
source: While this study showed that Sec17 could stimulate trans-SNARE paired membranes to fuse in a chemically defined reaction in the complete absence of Sec18, it was unclear whether such stimulation would be seen with physiological lipid composition and SNARE concentrations, since high SNARE levels can bypass and mask many fusion reaction requirements, such as for the Rab and even for HOPS (Mima et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Mima et al., 2008.

claim: A physiologically fluid lipid fatty acyl phase allows fusion at dramatically lower SNARE levels.
source: It has recently been reported (Zick and Wickner, 2016) that a physiologically fluid lipid fatty acyl phase allows fusion at dramatically lower SNARE levels.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Zick and Wickner, 2016.

claim: HOPS, Ypt7 and SNAREs can catalyze slow fusion at physiological protein levels and lipid compositions.
source: Though HOPS, Ypt7 and SNAREs can catalyze slow fusion at physiological protein levels and lipid compositions, we now report that this fusion is stimulated by Sec17 and Sec18:ATP without a need for ATP hydrolysis.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Fusion is blocked when the completion of SNARE domain zippering is prevented by deletion of 21 residues from the Qc-SNARE C-terminus.
source: Fusion is blocked when the completion of SNARE domain zippering is prevented by deletion of 21 residues (3 heptad repeats) from the Qc-SNARE C-terminus, but can be restored in a reaction that strictly requires Sec17, Sec18, and ATPγS.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Fusion blocked by Qc-3Δ can be restored in a reaction that strictly requires Sec17, Sec18, and ATPγS.
source: Fusion is blocked when the completion of SNARE domain zippering is prevented by deletion of 21 residues (3 heptad repeats) from the Qc-SNARE C-terminus, but can be restored in a reaction that strictly requires Sec17, Sec18, and ATPγS.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: In the fusion reaction with Qc-3Δ, the Sec17 apolar loop has functions in addition to membrane-binding.
source: In this fusion reaction, the Sec17 apolar loop has functions in addition to membrane-binding.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Proteoliposomes bearing prenylated Ypt7 at a 1:8000 molar ratio to lipids and SNAREs at 1:32,000 molar ratios to lipids represent physiological protein levels.
source: Proteoliposomes bearing prenylated Ypt7 at a 1:8000 molar ratio to lipids and SNAREs at 1:32,000 molar ratios to lipids were prepared with lipids of vacuolar head group composition and fatty acyl fluidity (Zick and Wickner, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Zick and Wickner, 2016 which established these as physiological levels.

claim: At the physiological Rab and SNARE levels employed, the rates of fusion resemble those seen with purified vacuoles.
source: At the physiological Rab and SNARE levels employed, the rates of fusion (Zick and Wickner, 2016) resemble those seen with purified vacuoles (Haas et al., 1994; Nichols et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Zick and Wickner, 2016; Haas et al., 1994; Nichols et al., 1997.

claim: When mixed with the soluble Qc-SNARE, proteoliposomes bearing either Ypt7:GTP and R-SNARE or Ypt7:GTP and QaQb-SNAREs undergo slow HOPS-dependent fusion.
source: When mixed with the soluble Qc-SNARE, proteoliposomes bearing either Ypt7:GTP and R-SNARE or Ypt7:GTP and QaQb-SNAREs undergo slow HOPS-dependent fusion (Figure 2A, filled vs open diamonds).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Fusion is stimulated by the addition of Sec17, Sec18, and ATP.
source: Fusion is stimulated by the addition of Sec17, Sec18, and ATP (filled circles).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Fusion for approximately the first 10 min was almost as rapid with Sec17, Sec18, and ATPγS as with ATP.
source: It is therefore noteworthy that fusion for approximately the first 10 min was almost as rapid with Sec17, Sec18, and ATPγS (Figure 2A, open circles; supplementary figures show average and standard deviations) as with ATP (filled circles).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The additional fusion at later times with ATP may be due to the recycling of post-fusion cis-SNARE complexes, allowing additional rounds of fusion.
source: The additional fusion at later times with ATP may be due to the recycling of post-fusion cis-SNARE complexes, allowing additional rounds of fusion.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that ATP supports more fusion than ATPγS at later time points.

claim: Hydrolyzable ATP is strictly required for the fusion of proteoliposomes prepared with all 4 SNAREs in cis-complexes.
source: In contrast to the capacity of ATPγS to support Sec17/Sec18 stimulation of the fusion of R- and QaQb- proteoliposomes, hydrolyzable ATP is strictly required for the fusion of proteoliposomes prepared with all 4 SNAREs in cis-complexes (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: ATP or ATPγS had no effect on the fusion mediated by HOPS alone.
source: While ATP or ATPγS had no effect on the fusion mediated by HOPS alone (data not shown), Sec17 gave a small stimulation (Figure 2A, filled triangles), as reported (Zick et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data (not shown) and citation to Zick et al., 2015.

claim: Sec17 gave a small stimulation of HOPS-mediated fusion.
source: While ATP or ATPγS had no effect on the fusion mediated by HOPS alone (data not shown), Sec17 gave a small stimulation (Figure 2A, filled triangles), as reported (Zick et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and citation to Zick et al., 2015.

claim: Sec18 without Sec17 stimulated HOPS-dependent fusion.
source: Sec18 without Sec17 also stimulated HOPS-dependent fusion (open triangles), and there was greater stimulation by Sec18 in the presence of ATP (filled squares) or ATPγS (open squares).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: There was greater stimulation by Sec18 in the presence of ATP or ATPγS.
source: Sec18 without Sec17 also stimulated HOPS-dependent fusion (open triangles), and there was greater stimulation by Sec18 in the presence of ATP (filled squares) or ATPγS (open squares).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Optimal initial rates of fusion required Sec17, Sec18, and ATP or ATPγS.
source: Optimal initial rates of fusion required Sec17, Sec18, and ATP or ATPγS.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The F21S,M22S mutation of Sec17 removes the apolar character of a loop of Sec17 near its N-terminus.
source: The F21S,M22S mutation of Sec17 removes the apolar character of a loop of Sec17 near its N-terminus (Winter et al., 2009), the L291A,L292A mutation near the C-terminus of Sec17 alters its interaction with Sec18 (Barnard et al., 1997; Schwartz and Merz, 2009), and a conserved lysyl residue at position 163 in αSNAP (corresponding to residue 159 and/or 163 in Sec17) is positioned near the SNARE complex zero-layer where it is important for functional interactions (Zhao et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Winter et al., 2009.

claim: The L291A,L292A mutation near the C-terminus of Sec17 alters its interaction with Sec18.
source: The F21S,M22S mutation of Sec17 removes the apolar character of a loop of Sec17 near its N-terminus (Winter et al., 2009), the L291A,L292A mutation near the C-terminus of Sec17 alters its interaction with Sec18 (Barnard et al., 1997; Schwartz and Merz, 2009), and a conserved lysyl residue at position 163 in αSNAP (corresponding to residue 159 and/or 163 in Sec17) is positioned near the SNARE complex zero-layer where it is important for functional interactions (Zhao et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Barnard et al., 1997; Schwartz and Merz, 2009.

claim: A conserved lysyl residue at position 163 in αSNAP (corresponding to residue 159 and/or 163 in Sec17) is positioned near the SNARE complex zero-layer where it is important for functional interactions.
source: The F21S,M22S mutation of Sec17 removes the apolar character of a loop of Sec17 near its N-terminus (Winter et al., 2009), the L291A,L292A mutation near the C-terminus of Sec17 alters its interaction with Sec18 (Barnard et al., 1997; Schwartz and Merz, 2009), and a conserved lysyl residue at position 163 in αSNAP (corresponding to residue 159 and/or 163 in Sec17) is positioned near the SNARE complex zero-layer where it is important for functional interactions (Zhao et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Zhao et al., 2015.

claim: Sec17-F21S,M22S was fully-functional for supporting Sec18-mediated SNARE complex disassembly for the fusion of 4-SNARE proteoliposomes.
source: In an earlier study at higher SNARE concentrations, Sec17-F21S,M22S was found to be fully-functional for supporting Sec18-mediated SNARE complex disassembly for the fusion of 4-SNARE proteoliposomes, but did not stimulate fusion of R- and Q-SNARE proteoliposomes in the absence of Sec18 (Zick et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Zick et al., 2015.

claim: Sec17-F21S,M22S did not stimulate fusion of R- and Q-SNARE proteoliposomes in the absence of Sec18.
source: In an earlier study at higher SNARE concentrations, Sec17-F21S,M22S was found to be fully-functional for supporting Sec18-mediated SNARE complex disassembly for the fusion of 4-SNARE proteoliposomes, but did not stimulate fusion of R- and Q-SNARE proteoliposomes in the absence of Sec18 (Zick et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Zick et al., 2015.

claim: Sec17-L291A,L292A was inactive in helping Sec18 to promote 4-SNARE proteoliposome fusion.
source: The opposite was true of Sec17-L291A,L292A; it was inactive in helping Sec18 to promote 4-SNARE proteoliposome fusion, but was fully active in promoting Sec18-independent fusion of either vacuoles or proteoliposomes (Schwartz and Merz, 2009; Zick et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Schwartz and Merz, 2009; Zick et al., 2015.

claim: Sec17-L291A,L292A was fully active in promoting Sec18-independent fusion of either vacuoles or proteoliposomes.
source: The opposite was true of Sec17-L291A,L292A; it was inactive in helping Sec18 to promote 4-SNARE proteoliposome fusion, but was fully active in promoting Sec18-independent fusion of either vacuoles or proteoliposomes (Schwartz and Merz, 2009; Zick et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Schwartz and Merz, 2009; Zick et al., 2015.

claim: Wild-type Sec17 can interact cooperatively with a mixture of vacuolar SNAREs without their membrane anchors, forming a 4sSNARE:oligo-Sec17 complex which binds to liposomes far more efficiently than either the sSNAREs alone or the Sec17 alone.
